name: Fibromuscular Dysplasia of the Cervical and Intracranial Arteries

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical features

criteria.description: Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance on angiography of affected arteries
Absence of atherosclerotic risk factors or lesions in affected vessels
Symptoms consistent with arterial stenosis, dissection, or aneurysm in cervical or intracranial arteries
Histological confirmation of medial fibroplasia or intimal fibroplasia if biopsy available

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic imaging findings plus clinical symptoms consistent with arterial involvement, excluding other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities such as catheter angiography, CT angiography, or MR angiography.

pathognomonic.symptomName: String of beads appearance on angiography
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic imaging finding diagnostic of FMD
searchTerms: string of beads look on angiogram

pathognomonic.notes: Common cause of stroke in young adults with FMD

common.notes: Due to arterial stenosis or embolism
Due to turbulent blood flow in affected arteries

common.symptomName: Neck pain localized to affected artery

occasional.notes: Resulting from arterial occlusion or embolism
Due to sympathetic chain involvement in cervical artery dissection

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances including transient monocular blindness
searchTerms: temporary vision loss in one eye

rare.notes: From rupture of intracranial aneurysms associated with FMD
Due to mass effect or ischemia
searchTerms: cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.symptomName: Hypertension secondary to renal artery involvement
searchTerms: high blood pressure from kidney artery
secondary high blood pressure from kidneys

laboratory: No specific laboratory markers; routine labs typically normal
imaging: Catheter angiography showing 'string of beads' pattern
CT angiography and MR angiography demonstrating arterial stenosis, aneurysms, or dissections
genetic: No definitive genetic mutation identified; possible familial clustering in some cases
other: Histopathology showing medial fibroplasia or intimal fibroplasia if biopsy performed

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of traditional cardiovascular risk factors
Plaque formation on imaging rather than 'string of beads'
Systemic symptoms such as fever and malaise
Histological evidence of vessel wall inflammation
Progressive stenosis of intracranial internal carotid arteries
Collateral vessel formation distinct from FMD

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe headache indicating possible arterial dissection or hemorrhage
Rapid progression of arterial stenosis or aneurysm formation
references: Olin JW, Gornik HL, Bacharach JM, et al. Fibromuscular Dysplasia: State of the Science and Critical Unanswered Questions: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association. Circulation. 2014;129(9):1048-1078.
